title: SkeinConfig.refresh() runs on NightConfig's file-watcher thread and empties the safety blacklists in place
claim: refresh() is wired to ModConfigEvent.Loading/Reloading (Skein.java:45-46), and FML dispatches Reloading synchronously from NightConfig's own daemon watcher thread, not the server thread. refresh() then does clear()-then-refill on Live.dimensionBlacklist (302-303) and Live.entityBlacklist (304-305), so there is a window in which those sets are observably empty while a tick is in flight. Both are consulted as safety gates: DimensionTicker.isExcluded (DimensionTicker.java:153-156) and EntityTicker.isPinned (EntityTicker.java:94-98, which short-circuits on isEmpty()).
scenario: An admin edits config/skein-common.toml while the server is running (the README's own remedy: "Turn phases off in this order if something is wrong"). NightConfig's FsWatcher thread wakes, ConfigTracker.loadConfig -> ModConfig.setConfig -> ModContainer.acceptEvent fires ModConfigEvent.Reloading on that thread, and Skein.onConfig -> refresh() executes concurrently with tickChildren. If the server thread evaluates isExcluded(minecraft:the_end) between line 302's clear() and line 303's re-add, the End is put in the `parallel` list and ticked on a worker even though the admin blacklisted it precisely because a mod ticks it unsafely. The same window on line 304 makes entityBlacklist.isEmpty() true, so a modded long-reach boss the user blacklisted (the documented remedy under "Reach beyond the margin") is placed into a parallel cell and ticks concurrently with work well inside its reach - invariant 1 broken with no diagnostic.
fix: Never mutate a published safety set in place. Change Live.dimensionBlacklist / entityBlacklist (and the resolved sets in resolveRegistries) to `volatile Set<...>` fields, build a fresh `Set.copyOf(...)` locally in refresh() and assign it in one store, so a reader sees either the whole old set or the whole new one. Better still, since none of these values need to change mid-tick: have onConfig() park the ModConfigSpec values in a pending flag and have Skein.onServerTickPre (which already runs on the server thread, between ticks) call refresh(), so no snapshot ever changes while a level is ticking.
evidence: Verified in bytecode: net/neoforged/fml/config/ConfigTracker.openConfig calls FileWatcher.defaultInstance().addWatch(path, new ConfigWatcher(...)) for every config type unless FMLConfig DISABLE_CONFIG_WATCHER is set; ConfigWatcher.run() calls ConfigTracker.loadConfig, whose tail is ModConfig.setConfig(...) -> ModContainer.acceptEvent(ModConfigEvent) - all synchronous on the caller. com/electronwill/nightconfig/core/file/FileWatcher constructs its own ThreadGroup and starts a daemon Thread running FsWatcher, so that caller is a dedicated watcher thread. SkeinConfig.java:302-309 is clear()-then-forEach(add) on ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet().

title: resolveRegionChunks under-clamps the cell size for 16-block spans; margins that are not a multiple of 16 silently push ~36% of randomly-ticked chunks back to serial
claim: The clamp computes needed = ceil(4*margin/16) chunks. For a span of width w the four-grid cover requires the two half-offset windows to meet, which in chunk units is C >= 4*ceil(margin/16), not C >= ceil(4*margin/16). Those differ whenever margin is not a multiple of 16. Points (entities, block entities) are unaffected; the 16-wide chunk spans that ChunkTicker.collect files (ChunkTicker.java:66) are not, so they fall through Grid.axis and land in Partition.serial - contradicting Partition.java:81 ("only happens when the configured cell is smaller than four margins, and the config clamp normally rules that out") and the README's "Raising it costs cell size, not coverage".
scenario: Set regions.marginBlocks = 40 (the README's documented remedy for modded content that reaches further than 32). needed = -floorDiv(-160,16) = 10, chunks = max(8,10) = 10, even, so regionBlocks = 160. Take the chunk at minX = 32 (span [32,48]): Grid.interior(32,48,0) needs 32-0 >= 40 -> false; Grid.interior(32,48,80) gives shifted = -48, start = -160, and start+160-(48-80) = 32 >= 40 -> false. axis() returns -1 and the chunk goes to the serial set. Per axis only 8 of the 10 chunk columns are interior to any grid (indices 2 and 7 are lost), so 1 - (8/10)^2 = 36% of randomly-ticked chunks run on the level-owning thread - in the phase the README measures at 8.4x overlap. Nothing logs it; /skein status just shows a larger `serial` count. Same for marginBlocks 33-47 and 49-63.
fix: Compute the clamp in chunk units so the widest span is accounted for: `int needed = MARGINS_PER_REGION * (-Math.floorDiv(-margin, 16));` (i.e. 4*ceil(margin/16), which is always even and needs no further rounding). At margin 32 and 48 this is identical to today's value; at 40 it yields 12 chunks instead of 10 and restores full coverage. Optionally assert the invariant at startup by test-placing a full period of chunk spans through Live.grid and warning if any is unplaceable.
evidence: Hand-evaluated Grid.interior/Grid.axis (core/Grid.java:49-61) over every chunk-aligned min in one period for margin 32 (all 8 covered), 40 (indices 2 and 7 uncovered), 33/36 (same two uncovered), 48 and 64 (all covered). ChunkTicker.collect passes minX..minX+16, so w = 16; EntityTicker.file and BlockEntityTicker.collect pass min==max, so w = 0 and points are unaffected.

title: Crash quarantine only gates the dimension phase, so a quarantined dimension keeps ticking on 16 threads
claim: `quarantined` is read in exactly one place - DimensionTicker.isExcluded (153-156). ChunkTicker.collecting (ChunkTicker.java:43-49), EntityTicker.run (EntityTicker.java:43-50), BlockEntityTicker.collecting (BlockEntityTicker.java:40-47) and ScheduledTickTicker.run (ScheduledTickTicker.java:61-68) gate only on pool/Live/SkeinCompat/profiler, never on the quarantine set. So the log line at 173-176 ("has been dropped back to serial ticking for the rest of this session") and the documented crashPolicy=DISABLE contract are both false: only the level's own tick() call moves back to the server thread, while its entity, random-tick and block-entity phases keep dispatching cell tasks to the pool.
scenario: Three dimensions, crashPolicy = DISABLE (the default). A chunk mod ships a C2ME-style async catcher that throws ConcurrentModificationException at the head of ServerChunkCache.tick - the exact case the README's "Known limits" describes as quarantining every parallel dimension on its first tick. tickOne catches it and adds the overworld to `quarantined`. From the next tick on, the overworld is in the `serial` list and ticks on the server thread, so ServerChunkCache.tick no longer trips the catcher and the error stops - but ServerLevel.tick still calls EntityTicker.run and BlockEntityTicker.finish, which still split the overworld across every worker. The admin sees one error, then silence, and reasonably concludes the dimension is now serial while it is in fact still the most parallel thing on the server. Conversely, when only two dimensions exist, quarantining one drops `parallel.size()` to 1, tickLevels returns false, and no dimension is threaded at all - yet all four in-level phases still are.
fix: Make the quarantine a level-wide kill switch: add `DimensionTicker.quarantined().contains(level.dimension())` to the gate in ChunkTicker.collecting, EntityTicker.run, BlockEntityTicker.collecting and ScheduledTickTicker.run, and add the level to `quarantined` from ParallelPass.runCell's DISABLE branch (ParallelPass.java:139-143) as well, so a phase that fails is actually disabled rather than logged once per item forever. Reword the message at DimensionTicker.java:173 to say what is actually being disabled.
evidence: grep for `quarantin` across src/main/java returns hits only in DimensionTicker (46, 57-63, 155, 172) and SkeinCommands (32, 68, 131-133); none of the four in-level tickers reference it. Verified in mcsrc that MinecraftServer.tickChildren (line 1051-1057) wraps only serverlevel.tick and rethrows as ReportedException, so the serial path has no extra containment either.

title: SkeinCompat.scan() is never re-run, so /skein reload can turn the Lithium guard off but never back on - and status confirms the wrong answer
claim: scan() is called exactly once, from Skein.onServerStarting (Skein.java:68). It reads SkeinConfig.Live.ignoreModConflicts at line 80 and, if true, returns leaving BLOCKED empty. SkeinCommands.reload (SkeinCommands.java:121-129) calls refresh() and resolveRegistries() but not scan(), and the file-watcher path calls only refresh(). So the value of general.ignoreModConflicts that matters is frozen at server start, while Live.ignoreModConflicts appears to change - and every readout the admin has agrees with the changed value rather than the frozen one.
scenario: Server starts with Lithium installed and general.ignoreModConflicts = true. scan() logs the warning and leaves BLOCKED empty, so all four in-level phases run. Later something misbehaves; the admin sets ignoreModConflicts = false and runs /skein reload. refresh() sets Live.ignoreModConflicts = false, the command replies "config re-read. Worker count changes apply on the next server start" (which names only the worker count as start-only), and /skein status then prints `phases: dimensions, scheduledTicks, randomTicks, entities, blockEntities` with no "(blocked)" marker and no warning block, because SkeinCompat.allows() still returns true for every phase and SkeinCompat.any() is false. The admin believes the protection is back on while all four phases are still running next to Lithium's alloc.chunk_random shared BlockPos and its world-border WeakHashMap - the failure modes this class exists to prevent.
fix: Call SkeinCompat.scan() from SkeinCommands.reload() (and from Skein.onConfig() when Skein.server() != null) so the guard is re-evaluated with the new flag. Because allows() is read from worker threads on hot gates, do not re-mutate the shared EnumMap in place: build an immutable EnumMap locally in scan() and publish it through a `private static volatile Map<Phase,String> blocked` field, so a re-scan is safely published and readers never observe a half-cleared map.
evidence: SkeinCompat.BLOCKED is a plain `private static final EnumMap` (line 50) mutated only in scan() (76-97); grep shows scan() has exactly one caller, Skein.java:68. SkeinCommands.reload (121-129) calls SkeinConfig.refresh() and SkeinConfig.resolveRegistries() only. SkeinCommands.phases()/append() and Skein.state() both derive their output from SkeinCompat.allows(), so the status text tracks BLOCKED, not Live.ignoreModConflicts.

title: An in-game config-file edit re-snapshots the id strings but never re-resolves them, so blockEntities/scheduledTicks blacklist changes silently do nothing
claim: refresh() refills only the *string* sets Live.blockEntityBlacklistIds (306-307) and Live.scheduledTickBlacklistIds (308-309). The sets the tickers actually consult - Live.blockEntityBlacklist (BlockEntityTicker.isPinned, BlockEntityTicker.java:85-95) and Live.scheduledTickBlacklist (ScheduledTickTicker.java:76) - are rebuilt only by resolveRegistries(), which has exactly two callers: Skein.onServerStarting (Skein.java:69) and SkeinCommands.reload (SkeinCommands.java:123). The file-watcher path calls neither, so editing the file is a no-op for precisely the two blacklists that exist for reach safety.
scenario: A tech modpack's machine reaches across the world from its block-entity tick - the failure mode the README calls "a genre, not an oddity". The admin adds `"themod:quarry"` to blockEntities.blacklist and saves config/skein-common.toml. FML's watcher fires, the log prints "Config file skein-common.toml changed, re-loading", refresh() updates blockEntityBlacklistIds, and Live.blockEntityBlacklist is untouched - so isPinned still returns false for the quarry and it keeps ticking in a parallel cell. Nothing in /skein status shows the blacklist contents, so the admin has no way to notice; the mitigation the README prescribes appears to have been applied and has not been. The same edit made through /skein reload does work, which makes the failure look intermittent.
fix: Call resolveRegistries() at the end of refresh() when the registries are populated (guard on Skein.server() != null, since refresh() also runs during mod loading before BuiltInRegistries is filled), logging the unknown-id list as onServerStarting does. Apply the same volatile-swap treatment as finding 1 so the resolved sets are replaced atomically rather than cleared at line 320/332 while a block-entity phase is reading them.
evidence: SkeinConfig.resolveRegistries() (319-351) is the only writer of Live.blockEntityBlacklist and Live.scheduledTickBlacklist; grep shows its only callers are Skein.java:69 and SkeinCommands.java:123. Skein.java:45-46 registers refresh() alone for ModConfigEvent.Loading/Reloading. The doc comment at SkeinConfig.java:267-271 explains why resolution is separate from refresh() but the reload path was never given the second half.

title: Holding pollTaskInternal for the whole dimension phase turns MinecraftServer.managedBlock into a permanent livelock
claim: `skein$holdTasksDuringPhase` cancels *all* of `pollTaskInternal` while `DimensionTicker.phaseActive()` is true. But `pollTaskInternal` has two halves, and only the second is the hazard the javadoc names. Vanilla (mcsrc/net/minecraft/server/MinecraftServer.java:863-876) is `if (super.pollTask()) return true; else { ... for (ServerLevel l : getAllLevels()) if (l.getChunkSource().pollTask()) return true; return false; }`. The first half drains the server's *own* `pendingRunnables` and is the only engine `BlockableEventLoop.managedBlock` has. Cancelling the whole method makes `MinecraftServer.pollTask()` return false unconditionally, so any `managedBlock` on the server thread during the phase can never make progress — and the server thread is *always* a participant in the phase, because `SkeinPool.invokeAll` line 147 has it run stolen level tasks.
scenario: Two or more parallel dimensions, so `DimensionTicker.tickLevels` sets `phaseActive = true` (DimensionTicker.java:122) and the server thread enters `invokeAll`'s steal loop. It polls the nether's `tickOne` task and runs it (SkeinPool.java:146-148). Inside that tick, a command block (not on any Skein blacklist — only scheduledTicks blacklists command blocks, and this is the blockEntities phase) executes `/reload`. That reaches `MinecraftServer.reloadResources` (mcsrc MinecraftServer.java:1547-1549): `if (this.isSameThread()) this.managedBlock(completablefuture::isDone);` — and `isSameThread()` is true, because this really is the server thread. `BlockableEventLoop.managedBlock` (mcsrc net/minecraft/util/thread/BlockableEventLoop.java:130-141) then loops `while (!isDone) { if (!pollTask()) waitForTasks(); }`. The future's continuation was scheduled with `thenAcceptAsync(..., this)` onto the server executor, so it can only complete via `super.pollTask()` — which the mixin has just made unreachable. `waitForTasks()` (BlockableEventLoop.java:144-147) does `Thread.yield(); LockSupport.parkNanos(100000L)` and the loop spins forever. `phaseActive` never clears (it is cleared in the `finally` at DimensionTicker.java:125-127, which this thread will never reach), so nothing can ever recover, and the stall watchdog cannot fire either — it lives in `invokeAll`'s wait loop (SkeinPool.java:158-161) and the server thread is stuck inside `task.run()`, one frame above it. Silent permanent hang, no log line. The same shape fires for any mod that calls `server.managedBlock(...)` from a level tick.
fix: Suppress only the half that is actually unsafe. Replace the `@Inject(method="pollTaskInternal", cancellable=true)` with a `@Redirect` on the `MinecraftServer.getAllLevels()` call inside `pollTaskInternal`, returning `List.of()` while `DimensionTicker.phaseActive()`. That leaves `super.pollTask()` — the server's own queue, and the only thing `managedBlock` can drive — working, while still keeping the server thread out of a `ChunkMap` a worker owns. If running queued `TickTask`s mid-phase is itself considered unacceptable, then the hold must at minimum be skipped when the event loop is inside a blocking wait, otherwise the server thread has no escape at all.
evidence: mcsrc/net/minecraft/server/MinecraftServer.java:863-876 (`pollTaskInternal` = `super.pollTask()` then per-level chunk-source polling); :829-830 (`managedBlock` override); :1547-1549 (`reloadResources` blocks on the server executor when `isSameThread()`). mcsrc/net/minecraft/util/thread/BlockableEventLoop.java:115-125 (`pollTask` drains `pendingRunnables`), :130-141 (`managedBlock` loop), :144-147 (`waitForTasks` = yield + 100us park). SkeinPool.java:146-148 (coordinator runs stolen tasks inline). DimensionTicker.java:122-127.

title: Nothing ever unparks the barrier waiter: every pass close pays 0-50us of pure sleep
claim: The README says the pool "waits by spinning briefly before parking, in both directions, and wakes only workers that are actually parked". Only one of those two directions has a wake. `wake()` (SkeinPool.java:196-207) unparks `TickContext.Worker`s whose `parked` flag is set; the coordinator waiting at the barrier is either the server thread (not a `Worker` at all) or a `Worker` whose `parked` flag is false while it sits in `invokeAll`'s loop. The wrapper that drives the count to zero (SkeinPool.java:128-134) only does `outstanding.decrementAndGet()` and then returns to `workerLoop`, which polls, finds nothing and goes to `awaitWork()`. It never signals the waiter. So after the ~256 `onSpinWait` budget is exhausted, the coordinator's only way out of the barrier is the 50us timer at line 157 expiring — it discovers `outstanding == 0` on average 25us after it actually became 0, and the park is subject to Linux timer slack on top.
scenario: The README's own measured workload: random ticks 4 passes, entities 4 passes, block entities 4 passes, plus the dimension barrier — 13 `invokeAll` closes per tick. Cells "finish microseconds apart", so the tail routinely outlives the ~1us spin budget and the coordinator parks at least once per barrier. 13 barriers x ~25us average = ~0.33ms of pure sleep per tick, worst case ~0.65ms. It is worst for the cheapest phase: block entities is measured at 0.41ms of wall across its 4 barriers, so timer granularity is a quarter to a half of that phase's entire wall clock — which is exactly why its overlap reads 1.77x rather than something near the worker count.
fix: Give the batch a waiter reference and signal it. Hoist the wrapper into a small class holding `AtomicInteger outstanding` and `volatile Thread waiter` (set to `Thread.currentThread()` before `wake(count)`), and in the wrapper's `finally` do `if (outstanding.decrementAndGet() == 0) { Thread w = waiter; if (w != null) LockSupport.unpark(w); }`. Keep the 50us timed park as the backstop so a missed signal still costs latency rather than a hang. The coordinator's loop needs no other change — it already re-checks `outstanding` after each park.
evidence: SkeinPool.java:128-134 (wrapper decrements and returns, no signal), :144-163 (wait loop, timed park at :157), :196-207 (`wake` only unparks `Worker`s with `parked == true`), TickContext.java:79 (`parked` is only set inside `awaitWork`, never while a Worker is coordinating a nested `invokeAll`). README measurement table: block entities 1.77x, 0.73ms in 0.41ms over 4 passes.

title: A throwable escaping a stolen task abandons the barrier and leaves undrained DeferredBuffers to be replayed next tick
claim: Every other place in the pool contains throwables: `workerLoop` wraps `task.run()` in `catch (Throwable)` (SkeinPool.java:73-80) precisely because "the pool silently shrinks to nothing and the barrier waits forever", and each body (`tickOne`, `runCell`, `runGroup`) catches per item. The coordinator's inline `task.run()` at line 147 is the one unguarded call. `outstanding` is safe — the wrapper decrements in a `finally` — but the *coordinator* is not: it unwinds out of `invokeAll` while its sibling tasks are still executing on workers, which is a direct violation of invariant 2 (the barrier is the only thing that makes level-wide structures read-only during a pass).
scenario: Any throwable out of a queued body while the coordinator happens to be the thread running it. The damage is not the exception, it is the unwind path: `ParallelPass.run` has no `try/finally` around `pool.invokeAll` (ParallelPass.java:79), so the pass's `cell.deferred().drain(level)` at :82-84 is skipped, the fatal-path `partition.release()` at :88 is skipped, and `EntityTicker.run` line 68 / `ChunkTicker.finish` / `BlockEntityTicker.finish`'s trailing `partition.release()` are all skipped too — none of them are in a `finally` either. The cells therefore survive with full DeferredBuffers. Next tick, `Partition.begin()` recycles them via `recycle()` (Partition.java:165-168), which clears `cell.items` but *not* `cell.deferred`, and the recycled cell goes back on the `spare` list. At that tick's barrier the coordinator drains it and replays last tick's parked work into the new one: `addFreshEntity` for entities that already spawned, `onMove`/`onRemove` on entities that have since moved or died, re-fired block events. `Partition.release()`'s own javadoc says exactly this must not happen ("must not be replayed into the next one") — but `release()` is the only method that clears `deferred`, and it is the one the unwind skips.
fix: Two lines and one line. In `SkeinPool.invokeAll`, wrap line 147 the same way `workerLoop` does: `try { task.run(); } catch (Throwable t) { Skein.LOGGER.error("Skein coordinator caught an unhandled throwable", t); }` — the coordinator must never leave the barrier early, whatever a stolen task does. Independently, make the recycling path safe by clearing the buffer too: add `cell.deferred.clear();` to `Partition.recycle()` (Partition.java:165-168), so a cell can never be reused carrying a previous tick's parked writes regardless of how the last tick exited.
evidence: SkeinPool.java:73-80 (workerLoop's guard, and the comment explaining why it exists) vs :146-149 (unguarded coordinator call). ParallelPass.java:79-91 (no try/finally around invokeAll; drain and release both on the normal path only). Partition.java:62-75 (`begin` calls `recycle`), :142-151 (`release` clears `deferred`), :165-168 (`recycle` clears `items` only). EntityTicker.java:68, ChunkTicker.java (`finish` tail), BlockEntityTicker.java:81 — every `partition.release()` is a trailing statement, not a `finally`. DeferredBuffer.java:91-105 (`drain` is the only other thing that empties the buffer).

title: The stall watchdog is blind to a hang in a task the coordinator itself is running
claim: `reportStall` is only reachable from inside `invokeAll`'s wait loop, i.e. it fires only when some thread is *waiting* at a barrier. But the pool's defining property is that the submitter helps: the coordinator spends most of a pass inside `task.run()` at line 147, not in the wait branch at 154-162. If the task the coordinator picked up is the one that hangs, no thread on the machine is in a wait loop — the workers are in `awaitWork()`, which has no watchdog at all — so the ten-second dump never happens. That is the exact failure the watchdog was written for: the README calls a stalled barrier "the worst failure this design has, because it looks exactly like the server hanging", and names the concrete cause (a corrupted `RECENT_TOGGLES` bucket chain spinning forever).
scenario: Dimension threading on with two levels. The server thread, as coordinator, steals the nether's `tickOne` (SkeinPool.java:147) and a redstone torch tick inside it spins forever on a corrupted `HashMap` chain — or hits the `managedBlock` livelock in finding 1. The other worker finishes the overworld and parks in `awaitWork`. Now `outstanding` is 1, but the only thread that would ever call `reportStall` is the stuck one. The server stops responding with no log output whatsoever, which is precisely the state the watchdog exists to make diagnosable. The same holds one level down: a coordinator stuck inside a stolen *cell* task hangs a phase silently.
fix: Make the deadline observable from outside the stuck thread. Keep a static `AtomicLong` of the oldest currently-open barrier's start (push on entry to `invokeAll`, pop on exit) and check it from a place that is still alive during the hang — either a single daemon watchdog thread started with the pool, or the existing `awaitWork()` timed-park path, which already wakes every 50ms and is exactly where the idle workers are during such a hang. On expiry, run the existing `reportStall` body (it already dumps every worker plus the caller) from whichever thread noticed, and name the coordinator thread in the message.
evidence: SkeinPool.java:144-163 — `reportStall` is called only from the `else` branch at :156-162, which is reached only when `queue.poll()` returned null and the coordinator is idling; :146-149 shows the coordinator spends the bulk of a pass inside `task.run()` instead. SkeinPool.java:84-106 — `awaitWork` has no elapsed-time check. SkeinPool.java:37-47 — the watchdog's own javadoc: "One thread that never returns from a task takes the whole tick loop with it."

title: resolveRegionChunks sizes the cell for a point, but random-ticked chunks are filed as a 16-block span, so whole classes of chunk column fall out of the parallel set
claim: The four-grid tiling covers a span of width w only when R >= 4m + 2w. resolveRegionChunks enforces only R >= 4m (MARGINS_PER_REGION = 4), which is the w = 0 case. ChunkTicker.collect files chunks with w = 16 (ChunkTicker.java:66), so for 112 of the 249 legal marginBlocks values the coverage proof fails for random ticks and those chunk columns are silently pushed into Partition.serial — exactly what the README says the config clamp exists to prevent ("the config raises the cell size to meet the margin rather than quietly pushing work back into the serial set").
scenario: Set marginBlocks = 40, leave chunkSize = 8. resolveRegionChunks returns needed = ceil(160/16) = 10, chunks = 10, so R = 160 and half = 80. Grid.interior accepts a chunk column iff m <= (minBlockX - offset) mod R <= R - m - 16, i.e. grid 0 accepts a in [40,104] and grid 1 accepts a in [0,24] union [120,160). Chunk columns sit at multiples of 16, so a = 32 and a = 112 satisfy neither: Grid.axis returns -1, Partition.place (Partition.java:86-88) files them serial. That is 2 of every 10 columns per axis, so 36% of every tick's randomly-ticked chunks run on the coordinator, every tick, with no log line and with /skein status still printing "cells: 10 chunks, 40-block margin". The whole ranges 33-40, 49-56, 65-72, 81-88, ... behave this way. At the documented minimum (chunkSize = 2, marginBlocks = 8 -> R = 32, half = 16) grid 0 accepts only a = 8 and grid 1 only a in [24,32), and no multiple of 16 is in either, so 100% of chunks are serial: parallelCount == 0, ParallelPass.run returns false, and the random-tick phase is pure overhead.
fix: Make the clamp aware of the widest footprint filed into the grid. After the existing even-rounding in resolveRegionChunks, bump until the chunk span fits: `while (16 * (Math.floorDiv(chunks * 8 - margin - 16, 16) + 1) < margin) chunks += 2;` (chunks*8 is half a cell in blocks; the expression is the smallest chunk-aligned offset above the left gap). Exhaustively checked over chunkSize in [2,64] x marginBlocks in [8,256]: zero uncovered chunk columns and zero uncovered points, the default (8,32) is unchanged at 8 chunks, and marginBlocks 33-40 becomes 12 chunks instead of a broken 10. The blunt alternative `needed = ceil((4*margin + 32)/16)` also works but costs the default cell (8 -> 10 chunks) for no reason.
evidence: Grid.java:56-61 interior() reduces to m <= r <= R-m-w with r = (min-offset) mod R. Union over offsets {0, R/2} leaves the gaps (R/2-m-w, m) and (R-m-w, R/2+m), empty only when R >= 4m+2w. Brute-forced the exact predicate (same floor arithmetic as Grid.interior) over the full config range: 3961 of 15687 (chunkSize, margin) pairs leave at least one chunk column uncovered; point footprints (w=0, integer and fractional coordinates) are uncovered in 0 of 15687. ChunkTicker.java:63-66 passes [minX, minX+16]; verified correct/conservative against Level.getBlockRandomPos (Level.java:1200-1203), which returns x + (i & 15), so the true footprint is [minX, minX+15].

title: PoiManager is unsynchronised, level-wide mutable state written from the parallel entity pass, and its 48-block reach is outside the margin
claim: Villager, raider, iron-golem and bee brain/goal code calls PoiManager directly from the entity tick. PoiManager extends SectionStorage, whose `storage` is a plain Long2ObjectOpenHashMap and whose `dirty` is a LongLinkedOpenHashSet, and both are mutated on those paths — including on what look like read-only queries. This is a seventh piece of vanilla per-level mutable tick-path state of the kind invariant 3 covers, and unlike the six already fixed it has no mixin at all (skein.mixins.json has no PoiManager/SectionStorage entry). The geometry cannot help: the POI scan radius is 48 > the 32-block default margin, and the structure is level-wide regardless of distance.
scenario: Two villages 300 blocks apart, one villager in each; both are interior to the same grid, so both tick in the same pass on two workers. Both run AcquirePoi (AcquirePoi.java:76): poimanager.findAllClosestFirstWithType(..., 48, HAS_SPACE) -> getInRange -> getInSquare -> getInChunk, which calls SectionStorage.getOrLoad (SectionStorage.java:78-92) once per section of a 9x9 chunk area (~1900 calls per scan). For any column not yet resident this runs readColumn, which does `this.storage.put(...)` for every section (SectionStorage.java:135-161) — and blocks on tryRead(chunkPos).join() inside the barrier. A put that triggers fastutil's rehash while the other worker is probing the same table leaves that worker spinning in the open-address probe loop: no exception, one thread never returns, the pass barrier never closes, server stops silently. That is the identical failure mode the README documents for RedstoneTorchBlock.RECENT_TOGGLES. Deterministic milder variant, no rehash needed: both villagers see the same unclaimed bed pass the HAS_SPACE filter and both call poimanager.take (AcquirePoi.java:85) -> PoiRecord.acquireTicket (PoiRecord.java:50-57), an unguarded `freeTickets--`, so two villagers claim one bed and the later ValidateNearbyPoi/VillagerMakeLove release throws IllegalStateException. Every take/release also runs SectionStorage.setDirty (SectionStorage.java:212-218) -> `this.dirty.add(key)` on a LongLinkedOpenHashSet from two threads, corrupting its link[] array.
fix: Treat SectionStorage the way RECENT_TOGGLES was treated: add a ReentrantLock field to SectionStorage via mixin and take it in get/getOrLoad/getOrCreate/setDirty/readColumn/writeColumn, and make PoiRecord.acquireTicket/releaseTicket synchronize on the owning PoiSection. It is a leaf lock — nothing under it re-enters the world — except readColumn's blocking disk read, which is why it is also worth pre-loading POI columns on the level thread. Stop-gap without a mixin: add minecraft:villager, minecraft:zombie_villager, minecraft:iron_golem, minecraft:bee and the raider types to the default entities.blacklist. Note the same structure is hit from the random-tick phase by ServerLevel.findLightningRod (ServerLevel.java:583-593), a 128-block PoiManager.findClosest reached from tickChunk's thunder branch (ServerLevel.java:484).

The block-change path (ServerLevel.onBlockStateChange, ServerLevel.java:1442-1457) is safe because it wraps its POI writes in getServer().execute(); the entity paths do not.

title: Default marginBlocks = 32 is smaller than vanilla's own largest single-tick write reach, so two same-pass write sets can overlap
claim: Invariant 1 needs every tick's write reach to be strictly less than the margin: two items in the same pass are separated by exactly 2*margin at worst (Grid.interior uses >= on both sides, so r = m and r = R-m are both legal), and a reach of r > m makes two such write sets overlap in a band 2(r-m) wide. The README states the margin only has to cover "follow range" for vanilla mobs, but several vanilla mobs have FOLLOW_RANGE above 32 and at least one of them writes to other entities out to that range: ZombifiedPiglin.alertOthers, at FOLLOW_RANGE = 35 inherited from Zombie.
scenario: Defaults: R = 128, m = 32, so pass 0 (grid offset 0) accepts positions with x mod 128 in [32,96]. Piglin P1 at x = 96 is interior to cell [0,128); piglin P2 at x = 160 is interior to cell [128,256). Both are in pass 0, on two workers, at the minimum legal separation of 64 = 2m. Both have a target and both reach maybeAlertOthers -> alertOthers (ZombifiedPiglin.java:142-152), which queries AABB.unitCubeFromLowerCorner(position).inflate(35, 10, 35): P1 covers x <= 131, P2 covers x >= 125. A third zombified piglin P3 at x = 130 has x mod 128 = 2, so it was filed into a different pass and is sitting idle — and it is inside both boxes. Both workers call P3.setTarget(target) simultaneously. ZombifiedPiglin.setTarget (ZombifiedPiglin.java:162-171) writes playFirstAngerSoundIn and ticksUntilNextAlert, calls setLastHurtByPlayer, then Mob.setTarget (Mob.java:245-250), which dispatches NeoForge's LivingChangeTargetEvent — so a third-party listener runs twice concurrently for one entity and P3 ends up with a target from one thread and anger timers from the other. The same 2(r-m) overlap band exists for every vanilla reach above 32: Zombie 35, WitherBoss 40, Llama 40, Villager/Bee/Allay/Blaze 48, EnderMan 64, Ghast 100 — and the villager's 48-block POI scan is the sharp case (see the PoiManager finding).
fix: Two options, both cheap. (a) Enforce the README's own rule at file time: in EntityTicker.isPinned (EntityTicker.java:80-99) add `if (entity instanceof Mob mob && mob.getAttributeValue(Attributes.FOLLOW_RANGE) > SkeinConfig.Live.borderMargin) return true;` — one attribute lookup per entity per tick, and it automatically covers modded mobs, which the current blacklist cannot. (b) Raise the default marginBlocks to 48 (resolveRegionChunks then yields a 12-chunk cell) and add minecraft:zombified_piglin, minecraft:enderman and minecraft:ghast to entities.blacklist. Separately, tighten Grid.interior's right-hand test to `>` (or document that reach must be strictly below margin), since as written two same-pass items can be exactly 2m apart and an entity at r = R-m writes into the first block of the next cell — which also breaks the "chunk-disjoint" half of invariant 1 for point-filed entities and block entities (the chunk-span path in ChunkTicker is safe, since its +16 makes the right-hand slack one block).
evidence: Zombie.createAttributes (Zombie.java:120-127) sets FOLLOW_RANGE 35; ZombifiedPiglin.createAttributes (ZombifiedPiglin.java:79-84) inherits it. ZombifiedPiglin.customServerAiStep calls maybeAlertOthers when getTarget() != null (ZombifiedPiglin.java:109-112), maybeAlertOthers calls alertOthers (:130-139), alertOthers inflates by getAttributeValue(FOLLOW_RANGE) in x and z and calls p.setTarget on every match (:142-152). Mob.setTarget fires CommonHooks.onLivingChangeTarget then assigns this.target (Mob.java:245-250). Grid.interior (Grid.java:56-61) uses >= on both bounds, so within one pass the closest two interior positions in adjacent cells are start+R-m and start+R+m, exactly 2m apart. Other vanilla FOLLOW_RANGE values grepped from net/minecraft/world/entity: Blaze 48, Villager 48, Bee 48, Allay 48, WitherBoss 40, Llama 40, EnderMan 64, Ghast 100.

title: Cross-dimension getChunk from a Skein-owned level tick hangs the server (nether/end portals)
claim: skein$currentOwner only grants ownership for the level the calling thread entered (TickContext.owns(this.level)). Any chunk access aimed at a *different* level therefore still fails vanilla's identity test and falls into ServerChunkCache.getChunk's off-thread branch (mcsrc ServerChunkCache.java:137-138), which does CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(..., this.mainThreadProcessor).join(). That queue is drained only by the server thread, and MinecraftServerMixin.skein$holdTasksDuringPhase (MinecraftServerMixin.java:76-81) makes MinecraftServer.pollTaskInternal return false for the whole duration of the dimension phase — so the join can never complete. Cross-level chunk access from a level tick is not a mod-only pattern: it is the vanilla portal path.
scenario: Default config (dimensions=true, entities=true), overworld + nether. DimensionTicker.tickLevels queues one Runnable per level into SkeinPool (DimensionTicker.java:118-124); with 3 dimensions the server thread steals one and Skein Workers take the rest, so the overworld is ticked by a Worker W. A pig (or a player — players are pinned to the serial tail but still run on W) stands in a nether portal. Entity.tick -> baseTick -> handlePortal (mcsrc Entity.java:448, 2270-2282) -> NetherPortalBlock.getPortalDestination (mcsrc NetherPortalBlock.java:130-141) resolves `serverlevel` = the NETHER, then getExitPortal -> PortalForcer.findClosestPortalPosition -> `this.level.getBlockState(p)` on the nether (mcsrc PortalForcer.java:49) -> netherChunkSource.getChunk(x, z, FULL, true). On W, TickContext.owns(netherLevel) is false (worker.local.level is the overworld), so skein$currentOwner hands back this.mainThread, `Thread.currentThread() != mainThread` is true, and W blocks forever in join(). W never returns from its task, SkeinPool.invokeAll's outstanding counter never reaches 0 (SkeinPool.java:144-163), the dimension barrier never closes, and the server stops with no crash. If the in-level entity phase is open, W is also holding the nether's skein$chunkLoadLock (line 223-228) while blocked, so the nether's own coordinator wedges on the next chunk load too. SkeinPool.reportStall dumps the stacks after 10s but nothing recovers.
fix: Stop routing non-owned levels down vanilla's off-thread path. Minimum viable fix: in skein$guardChunkFetch and skein$guardChunkFuture, detect `TickContext.current() != null && TickContext.current() != this.level`, and for that case take the *target* level's skein$chunkLoadLock and run the body inline; correspondingly widen skein$currentOwner to `TickContext.current() != null ? Thread.currentThread() : this.mainThread` so the inline branch is actually taken. That removes the hang and puts cross-level chunk-system access under the target level's lock. The deeper fix is to notice cross-level entry at all (a `TickContext.current() != this.level` probe on the chunk source / Level.getBlockState) and quarantine the target dimension out of the parallel set for the rest of the session, since the same call also writes blocks into the other level (PortalForcer.createPortal, EndPlatformFeature.createEndPlatform) with no protection at all.
evidence: ServerChunkCacheMixin.java:156-158 (owns(this.level) only); :186 and :223-228 (lock is this.level's, original.call still hits the redirect); mcsrc/net/minecraft/server/level/ServerChunkCache.java:137-138 (supplyAsync(...).join()); mcsrc/.../BlockableEventLoop.java:88-91 (tell + unpark of getRunningThread, which MainThreadExecutor.getRunningThread pins to ServerChunkCache.this.mainThread); MinecraftServerMixin.java:76-81 (pollTaskInternal forced to false while phaseActive); DimensionTicker.java:118-127; SkeinPool.java:115-163; mcsrc/net/minecraft/world/entity/Entity.java:448, 2270-2282; mcsrc/net/minecraft/world/level/block/NetherPortalBlock.java:130-148; mcsrc/net/minecraft/world/level/portal/PortalForcer.java:49, 127-147.

title: UNKNOWN ticket for another dimension is parked in the wrong level's buffer and replayed concurrently with that level's tick
claim: skein$parkTicket calls DeferredWork.defer(this.level, ...), but DeferredWork.defer ignores its `level` argument entirely (DeferredWork.java:34-42, 68-70): it parks into whatever DeferredBuffer the *calling thread* currently holds. The gate at line 186 is `local.deferring`, which is a thread property, not a per-level one, so a worker deferring for level A that takes the published fast path on level B's chunk source parks a level-B DistanceManager.addTicket into a level-A cell buffer. ParallelPass then replays it on level A's coordinator at level A's barrier (ParallelPass.java:82-84) — while level B is being ticked concurrently by its own thread. DistanceManager.addTicket mutates Long2ObjectOpenHashMap `tickets` via getTickets(chunkPos) and then ChunkTicketTracker.update, none of which is synchronised.
scenario: dimensions=true and entities=true (both defaults), overworld + nether. A mob in the overworld's entity pass enters a nether portal; the nether-side destination chunk *is* already loaded at FULL (a player is on the other side), so the fast path at lines 209-219 succeeds instead of deadlocking as in the previous finding. `load` is true (Level.getBlockState uses requireChunk=true), so skein$parkTicket queues `netherDistanceManager.addTicket(UNKNOWN, pos, 33, pos)` into the overworld cell's DeferredBuffer. Milliseconds later the overworld coordinator drains that buffer and runs addTicket against the nether's DistanceManager at the same moment the nether's owning thread is inside purgeStaleTickets / runAllUpdates / addTicket on the same maps. Classic unsynchronised Long2ObjectOpenHashMap interleaving: a resize during a concurrent get returns the wrong SortedArraySet or none, and a lost ticketTracker.update leaves a chunk's level wrong — the chunk unloads while entities are standing in it, or is never released. Failure is silent, exactly the RECENT_TOGGLES failure mode the README describes.
fix: Make the deferral target level-aware. Either (a) have skein$parkTicket check `TickContext.current() == this.level` and, when it is not, apply the ticket inline while holding that level's skein$chunkLoadLock instead of parking it; or (b) give DeferredWork.defer teeth — compare the passed `level` against TickContext.current() and refuse to park (run inline / route to the target level's own barrier) when they differ. Given finding #1, the clean answer is to make the whole cross-level branch explicit in skein$guardChunkFetch and never reach skein$parkTicket with `this.level != TickContext.current()`.
evidence: ServerChunkCacheMixin.java:213 and :240-245; DeferredWork.java:34-42 (the `level` parameter is never read) and :68-70 (target() uses only TickContext.buffer()); TickContext.java:147-153 (deferring() is per-thread, not per-level); ParallelPass.java:82-84 (drain on the coordinator of *this* level between passes); mcsrc/net/minecraft/server/level/DistanceManager.java:42-43 (plain Long2ObjectOpenHashMap tickets), :152-164 (addTicket -> getTickets + ticketTracker.update), :68-92 (purgeStaleTickets iterating the same map).

title: Negative getChunk(..., load=false) lookups always take the level-wide chunk lock during a pass
claim: ChunkSlots never stores a null result (put is guarded by `published != null` at :212 and `result != null` at :229), and the published fast path only returns when getChunkIfPresent is non-null. So a lookup whose answer is legitimately "not loaded" can never be cached and never short-circuits: it falls through to `lock.lock()` and the full vanilla call on every single invocation. Vanilla does cache the negative — storeInCache is reached with a null chunk and the 4-entry loop returns it via `chunkaccess != null || !requireChunk` (mcsrc ServerChunkCache.java:145-150, 165). Skein additionally cancels storeInCache while deferring (:168-173), so it removes vanilla's negative cache and puts a level-wide ReentrantLock in its place. Vanilla's own body proves the lock is unnecessary here: with requireChunk=false and chunkAbsent true, getChunkFutureMainThread adds no ticket and returns the already-completed UNLOADED_CHUNK_FUTURE, managedBlock's loop body never executes, and the method returns null with zero side effects.
scenario: An entity ticks in a cell at the edge of the loaded/force-loaded region (the README's own benchmark is a 1024-chunk force-loaded square, so its border is ~128 chunks long). Entity.move -> Level.getCollisions -> BlockCollisions.computeNext -> Level.getChunkForCollisions(cx, cz) -> getChunk(cx, cz, ChunkStatus.FULL, false) (mcsrc Level.java:895-897, BlockCollisions.java:59, 66-80). The entity's inflated AABB straddles a chunk boundary whose neighbour is outside the loaded area, and BlockCollisions' single-entry cachedBlockGetter thrashes as the Cursor3D alternates between the two columns, so the null column is re-asked many times per sweep, and move()/noCollision()/checkInsideBlocks each run a sweep. Every one of those calls now serialises on ((SkeinLevel) level).skein$chunkLoadLock() — the one lock every worker in the level shares. A handful of border entities is enough to collapse the pass's overlap factor to ~1x for everyone, and local.chunkLockNanos will show it.
fix: Short-circuit the absent case before taking the lock, mirroring vanilla's chunkAbsent test exactly. After the currentlyLoading check in skein$guardChunkFetch, add: `if (!load && (holder == null || holder.getTicketLevel() > ChunkLevel.byStatus(status))) { return null; }`. This is bit-for-bit what vanilla returns for that input (mcsrc ServerChunkCache.java:246-248 -> UNLOADED_CHUNK_FUTURE, already completed, no ticket, no runDistanceManagerUpdates), and it must NOT be extended to the case where the holder is present at a sufficient ticket level but the status future is not yet done — that one can still start generation via scheduleChunkGenerationTask and has to keep going under the lock.
evidence: ServerChunkCacheMixin.java:201-237 (no null caching, unconditional fallthrough to lock at :223) and :168-173 (storeInCache cancelled, removing vanilla's negative cache); ChunkSlots.java:78-89 (put has no null path); mcsrc/net/minecraft/server/level/ServerChunkCache.java:144-151 (vanilla's negative-cache hit), :162-166 (storeInCache of null when !requireChunk), :227-249 (requireChunk=false skips addTicket and runDistanceManagerUpdates; chunkAbsent -> UNLOADED_CHUNK_FUTURE), :159 (managedBlock returns immediately on an already-done future); mcsrc/net/minecraft/world/level/Level.java:893-897; mcsrc/net/minecraft/world/level/BlockCollisions.java:51-80.

title: Block.capturedDrops is only made per-thread while deferring(), so dimension-tick threads share the vanilla static
claim: BlockMixin picks between the thread-local SKEIN_DROPS and the vanilla static on TickContext.deferring() (line 53 for the read, line 61 for the write). deferring() is only true inside an in-level parallel pass: DimensionTicker.tickOne enters with TickContext.enter(level, false, null) (DimensionTicker.java:164), so it is false for the whole of ServerLevel.tick() on every dimension worker. Every other piece of state gated this way (Level.randValue, Level.captureBlockSnapshots, capturedBlockSnapshots, restoringBlockSnapshots, the neighbour updater, Level.random) is per-level, so one thread per level makes the fallback safe. capturedDrops is not: mcsrc Block.java:555 declares it `private static List<ItemEntity> capturedDrops`, one field for the whole server. With dimensions.enabled = true (the default) two workers ticking different dimensions therefore share one capture bracket, which is exactly the failure the mixin's own javadoc describes.
scenario: Overworld and nether both parallel (>=2 non-blacklisted dimensions, so DimensionTicker.tickLevels runs). In the same server tick the overworld breaks a block that drops (e.g. SugarCaneBlock.java:46 -> Level.destroyBlock -> Level.java:329 Block.dropResources, or Block.java:181 updateOrDestroy when a torch/plant loses its support), and the nether does the same (nether wart popping off soul sand, a piston at PistonBaseBlock.java:331, fire/lava destroying a block). Interleaving: T_over beginCapturingDrops() -> static = listO; T_nether beginCapturingDrops() -> static = listN (listO orphaned); T_over popResource() -> listN.add(overworld ItemEntity); T_over stopCapturingDrops() -> returns listN, static = null; T_over CommonHooks.handleBlockDrops(overworldLevel, ..., listN) -> overworldLevel.addFreshEntity(...) on entities constructed against the nether (CommonHooks.java:543); T_nether popResource() -> capturedDrops == null so it spawns straight into the world with no BlockDropsEvent at all (Block.java:365-370); T_nether stopCapturingDrops() -> returns null; T_nether handleBlockDrops(..., drops=null, ...) -> BlockDropsEvent stores the null list verbatim and CommonHooks.java:542 `for (ItemEntity entity : event.getDrops())` throws NullPointerException. Under crashPolicy=DISABLE that silently quarantines the nether to serial ticking for the session; under RETHROW it crashes the server. The milder interleaving (both threads adding to the same ArrayList) silently duplicates or loses drops and hands one break's items to the other break's BlockDropsEvent listeners.
fix: Gate on being inside any Skein-owned level tick rather than on deferral, using the *same* predicate in both handlers so a bracket is never opened on the static and closed on the thread-local: `TickContext.current() != null ? SKEIN_DROPS.get() : capturedDrops` at line 53, and `if (TickContext.current() != null) SKEIN_DROPS.set(drops); else capturedDrops = drops;` at line 61. Since capturedDrops is `private static` in Block and unreachable from anywhere else in mcsrc, unconditionally using SKEIN_DROPS is also correct and cheaper than the branch. Note the GETSTATIC redirect also lists beginCapturingDrops as a target, which contains only a PUTSTATIC (Block.java:562-564) and so contributes no injection point; drop it from that list while you are there.
evidence: mcsrc net/minecraft/world/level/block/Block.java:555 `private static List<ItemEntity> capturedDrops = null;` (static, not per-level); Block.java:562-574 begin/stopCapturingDrops; Block.java:361-371 popResource reads/writes it. skein core/DimensionTicker.java:164 `TickContext.State previous = TickContext.enter(level, false, null);` and TickContext.java:118 `local.deferring = deferring && buffer != null;` -> deferring() is false for the entire dimension-parallel level tick. A grep of every `TickContext.deferring()` call site in the mod shows BlockMixin.java:53/61 is the only one guarding *static* rather than per-level state. mcsrc CommonHooks.java:538-551 handleBlockDrops iterates event.getDrops() without a null check; BlockDropsEvent's constructor stores the list as given.

title: Vanilla portal transit writes into another dimension from an entity tick, and neither the deferral buffer nor the dimension barrier covers it
claim: DeferredWork.defer(Level level, Runnable action) ignores its `level` argument entirely and always parks the action in the *calling thread's* buffer, which is drained at the calling level's barrier (ParallelPass.java:79). ServerLevelMixin.skein$deferSpawn (line 71) passes the destination level as `self` and relies on that argument being honoured. It is not. Worse, under pure dimension threading deferring() is false, so the write is applied inline on the wrong level's thread with no deferral at all. This is not a mod-only hazard as the README's 'Mods that tick one dimension from another' limit suggests: vanilla portal travel does exactly this from inside Entity.baseTick.
scenario: dimensions.enabled + entities.enabled (both default true), overworld and nether both ticking on Skein workers. A pig walks into a nether portal. Its tick runs on the overworld's worker: Entity.java:448 baseTick -> handlePortal -> Entity.java:2282 changeDimension -> Entity.java:2745 `serverlevel1.addDuringTeleport(entity2)` -> ServerLevel.java:907-912 -> private addEntity, which skein$deferSpawn intercepts and parks in the overworld cell's DeferredBuffer. The overworld's pass barrier then runs `netherLevel.addFreshEntity(pig)` on the overworld coordinator while the nether worker is concurrently inside its own tick, mutating PersistentEntitySectionManager's knownUuids HashSet, EntityLookup's byId/byUuid maps and EntitySectionStorage's section map. Two threads in an unsynchronised HashMap: the pig vanishes, or a bucket chain corrupts and a later lookup spins forever inside HashMap.get, which is the silent-freeze signature the README already attributes to RECENT_TOGGLES. The same call path also reaches PortalForcer via getPortalDestination (Entity.java:2277), which can setBlockAndUpdate obsidian and portal blocks into the nether from the overworld thread, and Skein's margin geometry says nothing about a block write in a different dimension. With randomTicks/entities disabled the deferral is skipped and netherLevel.addEntity runs inline on the overworld thread, which is the same race without the barrier delay.
fix: Make cross-level structural writes leave the calling thread. In DeferredWork.defer, when `level != TickContext.current()`, do not use the caller's buffer: hand the action to `level.getServer().execute(action)` (the server's ConcurrentLinkedQueue task list, which vanilla itself already uses for exactly this reason at ServerLevel.java:1448-1455 for POI updates) so it runs on the server thread after the dimension barrier has closed. Apply the same test in ServerLevelMixin.skein$deferSpawn (line 69) so the check holds when deferring() is false. For the block-writing half, wrap Entity.handlePortal (or Entity.changeDimension) so that when TickContext.current() != null and the transition crosses dimensions the whole transition is posted to server.execute rather than run on the ticking thread; a one-tick delay on portal transit is unobservable and it is the only way the destination level's chunks and entity registry are quiescent when they are touched.
evidence: skein core/DeferredWork.java:34-42 — the `level` parameter is never read; target() at :68-70 returns TickContext.buffer(), the caller's buffer. skein mixin/ServerLevelMixin.java:67-74 passes the destination level to that ignored parameter. skein core/ParallelPass.java:79 `deferred += cell.deferred().drain(level);` drains into the *calling* level's barrier. skein core/DimensionTicker.java:164 gives deferring() == false for the whole dimension-parallel tick. mcsrc net/minecraft/world/entity/Entity.java:448 handlePortal() inside baseTick; Entity.java:2270-2290 handlePortal calls changeDimension inline with no server.execute; Entity.java:2745 `serverlevel1.addDuringTeleport(entity2);`; mcsrc net/minecraft/server/level/ServerLevel.java:907-912 addDuringTeleport -> addEntity; ServerLevel.java:939-947 addEntity -> entityManager.addNewEntity. Contrast ServerLevel.java:1443-1456, where vanilla deliberately routes POI updates through getServer().execute().

title: Deferred structural writes are routed by the running thread, not by the level they target
claim: `defer(Level level, Runnable action)` accepts a `Level` and never uses it; `target()` (line 68-70) picks the buffer purely from `TickContext` — i.e. from whichever level the *calling thread* is ticking. Every deferral site is likewise gated on the thread predicate `TickContext.deferring()` rather than on `TickContext.current() == theLevelBeingWritten` (ServerLevelMixin:69/79/113, LevelMixin:283/295, LevelTicksMixin:75-85, ServerChunkCacheMixin:244). So a tick on level A that performs a structural write on level B parks it in A's cell buffer, and `ParallelPass:83` replays it on A's thread at A's barrier — while B is being ticked concurrently by another worker (dimension threading is on by default). Invariant 2 ("during a parallel pass the entity registry is READ-ONLY, every structural write is replayed by the coordinator") holds only for the coordinator of the level that owns the write; here the wrong coordinator applies it.
scenario: Overworld and Nether both ticking in parallel. A zombie / minecart / primed TNT with no passengers (so `EntityTicker.isPinned` is false) stands in a nether portal and is ticked in an Overworld cell. `Entity.baseTick` (mcsrc Entity.java:448) -> `handlePortal()` (Entity.java:2270) -> `changeDimension(transition)` -> `serverlevel1.addDuringTeleport(entity2)` (Entity.java:2745) -> `ServerLevel.addEntity` -> `ServerLevelMixin.skein$deferSpawn` sees `deferring()==true` and parks `() -> netherLevel.addFreshEntity(entity2)` into the *Overworld* cell's DeferredBuffer, returning `true` to the caller. At the Overworld's entity-phase barrier that lambda runs `PersistentEntitySectionManager.addEntityWithoutEvent` against the **Nether's** structures: `EntitySectionStorage.sections` (Long2ObjectOpenHashMap), `sectionIds` (LongAVLTreeSet), `EntityLookup.byId` (Int2ObjectLinkedOpenHashMap) and `byUuid`/`knownUuids` (plain HashSets), `entityTickList`, `navigatingMobs`, `ChunkMap.entityMap`. The Nether's own coordinator is at that same instant draining its own buffers into exactly those maps. Two writers on a fastutil open-hash map: a resize concurrent with a `put`/`computeIfAbsent` leaves a broken bucket chain, which surfaces later as a `getSection`/`getEntity` probe that never terminates (a barrier that never closes — the silent hang the README describes) or as an entity that is simply never registered and vanishes. `ServerChunkCacheMixin.skein$parkTicket` (line 244) has the same defect: it parks a ticket for `this.level` into whatever buffer the current thread happens to hold, so a cross-level `getChunk` (which portal search does constantly) adds a ticket to the destination level's DistanceManager from the source level's barrier.
fix: Make the buffer selection level-aware. Change `DeferredWork.target(Level level)` to return the current thread's buffer only when `level == TickContext.current()`; otherwise the write does not belong to this barrier. For the mismatch case either (a) hand the entry to a per-level `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` on the *target* level that its own coordinator drains at its own barrier (the cheap, correct option — cross-level writes are rare so the CAS cost is irrelevant), or (b) run it inline under a per-level structural lock. title: Component join tests the Y axis, so two components can share a chunk and race LevelChunk's unsynchronised per-chunk state
claim: ScheduledTickTicker.java:70-74 sets link = 2*margin+16 with the explicit stated intent that "two ticks whose write zones could share a chunk must not run at once", because "cells in the grid split are chunk-aligned and get this for free, components are not". But withinLink() (ClusterPartition.java:213-217) requires the gap to be <= link on X *and* Y *and* Z. A chunk is a 2D column: two ticks separated only in Y are in the same chunk no matter how far apart they are vertically, yet the Y term makes them separate components that run concurrently. The +16 buys nothing on the Y axis, and Partition/Grid (Grid.java, x/z only) has no equivalent hole, so this is specific to the scheduled-tick split.
scenario: Default config (margin 32 -> link 80). One chunk column contains a redstone/hopper sorter at y=100 and a second redstone floor at y=-50 (a sky base over a deep base — or just a surface water lake over a cave lava pool, which is the common natural case). Delta Y = 150 > 80 and delta X = delta Z = 0, so gap() returns 0 on X and Z but 150 on Y, withinLink returns false, joinNeighbours never unions them, and finish() emits two Groups that ScheduledTickTicker:105 hands to pool.invokeAll on two threads. Both sides call Level.setBlock -> LevelChunk.setBlockState on the *same* LevelChunk object. Every such call hits this.heightmaps.get(...).update(...) (LevelChunk.java:254-257), whose setHeight goes to SimpleBitStorage.set (SimpleBitStorage.java:288-295) — `this.data[i] = j & ~(mask<<k) | value<<k`, a read-modify-write of a long that packs 7 columns, so one thread's update is silently lost and the wrong heightmap is broadcast and saved. Worse, as soon as either side touches a block-entity block — a comparator flipping (ComparatorBlock.tick -> setBlock -> LevelChunk.setBlockState:286-301 -> getBlockEntity -> this.blockEntities.get(pos), then updateBlockEntityTicker -> this.tickersInLevel.compute/remove), or fire/lava/water destroying a chest or sign (LevelChunk.removeBlockEntity:439-449 -> this.blockEntities.remove(pos)) — two threads are structurally mutating the chunk's `blockEntities` (Object2ObjectOpenHashMap, ChunkAccess.java:82) and `tickersInLevel` (plain java.util.HashMap, LevelChunk.java:75). A fastutil open-addressing remove() runs shiftKeys() over the table while the other thread is walking a probe chain in get(): the walk never terminates, the worker never returns, SkeinPool's barrier never closes, and the server hangs with no exception — the exact silent-freeze signature the README attributes to the unreproduced 0-tick redstone report.

Concretely: in bucket() (ClusterPartition.java:250-252) pass a constant 0 for the y bucket coordinate, and in withinLink() (line 215) delete the Y term, leaving the X and Z gap tests. joinNeighbours' dy loop then degenerates harmlessly. Cost: a deep flow and a surface flow in the same column become one component (they already have to be, for the chunk argument to hold); benefit: the invariant the +16 was chosen for actually holds. If per-Y parallelism is wanted later it has to be earned by proving no shared per-chunk state, which LevelChunk.heightmaps/blockEntities/tickersInLevel/gameEventListenerRegistrySections currently disprove.

title: RedStoneWireBlock.shouldSignal is unsynchronised mutable state on a singleton, written by every wire power recalculation
claim: Invariant 3 lists four pieces of vanilla/NeoForge per-level or static mutable tick-path state that were found and fixed. There is a fifth, and it is on the hottest path this phase has: RedStoneWireBlock.shouldSignal (mcsrc RedStoneWireBlock.java:88) is a plain non-final instance field on the Blocks.REDSTONE_WIRE singleton, shared by every wire in every dimension. calculateTargetStrength sets it false, calls level.getBestNeighborSignal(pos), then sets it back to true (RedStoneWireBlock.java:322-324) — a classic single-threaded bracket. Skein has no mixin for it (skein.mixins.json lists RedstoneTorchBlockMixin but no wire mixin; `grep -rn shouldSignal src/` returns nothing).
scenario: Two redstone contraptions 200 blocks apart become two ClusterPartition groups and run concurrently at ScheduledTickTicker:105. In each, a repeater/comparator/torch scheduled tick calls level.setBlock (DiodeBlock.java:55-62, RedstoneTorchBlock.tick), whose LevelChunk.setBlockState calls state.onPlace -> DiodeBlock.updateNeighborsInFront -> level.neighborChanged -> RedStoneWireBlock.neighborChanged (:404-407) -> updatePowerStrength -> calculateTargetStrength. Interleaving: thread A executes `shouldSignal = false` and enters getBestNeighborSignal; thread B enters, runs its own bracket, and executes `shouldSignal = true` (line 324) while A is still inside the loop. A's remaining getSignal calls now see shouldSignal == true, so getSignal (line 438-450) returns the neighbouring wire's POWER instead of 0 and isSignalSource (line 474) reports the wire as a source. A computes i = 15 instead of the true non-wire best signal, and returns Math.max(i, j-1) = 15 rather than 14: the wire stops decaying. From then on each wire in that line reads its still-15 neighbour as a full source, so the line stays at 15 after the lever is cut, and updatePowerStrength -> setBlock -> updateNeighborsAt -> neighborChanged -> updatePowerStrength recurses until the per-thread CollectingNeighborUpdater chain cap stops it — a stuck-on circuit plus a tick spent burning the whole update budget. The mirror interleaving (B sets false while A is inside a torch's or door's hasNeighborSignal) makes a live wire report 0 and spuriously flips unrelated components. This is dimension-threading-visible too, since the field is one object for the whole server.

A per-thread copy is preferable to a lock here because getBestNeighborSignal calls back into arbitrary block code.

title: The scheduledTicks blacklist can never match a structure block — it is triggered from neighborChanged, never from a scheduled tick
claim: The fallback at ScheduledTickTicker.java:75-81 scans only `tick.type()` of the ticks collected this tick, and the documented purpose of the `minecraft:structure_block` entry (SkeinConfig.java:87-98, README "Ticks whose reach nothing bounds ... structure blocks ... one of them anywhere in a tick's collected set sends the whole set back through vanilla's serial loop") is to keep unbounded structure placement out of the parallel path. Result is either a silently lost mapping (a fresh, differently seeded RandomSequence is created next tick, so loot stops being reproducible from the save) or an ArrayIndexOutOfBounds / infinite probe loop inside a worker -- a barrier that never closes, the same silent-hang signature the README documents for RECENT_TOGGLES. If W2 is writing that same section, vanilla's ThreadingDetector fires 'Accessing PalettedContainer from multiple threads'; if it is writing a different section of the same chunk, the two silently race that chunk's Heightmaps and unsaved flag. Immediately after, W1 calls netherLevel.addDuringTeleport(entity): with in-level phases on this is parked into the OVERWORLD's DeferredBuffer and applied by the overworld coordinator while the nether is mid-tick, so entityManager.addNewEntity writes the nether's entity-id map and EntitySectionStorage while the nether's own entity pass is reading them; with in-level phases off (deferring()==false) it just runs inline on W1, same result. Symptom is a mob arriving in the nether with a duplicated or missing id, or 'Fetching addPacket for removed entity' -- a failure the item-count and armour-stand tests could not catch because nothing in them crossed a portal.
fix: Make cross-level work leave the source level's thread. Preferred: inject at Entity.changeDimension HEAD and, when transition.newLevel() != TickContext.current(), park the entire call via MinecraftServer.execute so it runs after the dimension barrier closes; also pin any entity whose portalProcess is non-null in EntityTicker.isPinned. Minimum viable: fix DeferredWork.defer to honour its 'level' argument -- when level != TickContext.current(), route the action to a per-target-level queue that DimensionTicker drains on the server thread after the dimension barrier rather than into the calling cell's buffer. Pinning alone is not sufficient, because the pinned tail still runs on the source level's coordinator while the other dimension ticks, so the target-level queue is the necessary half.

title: Raid.groupRaiderMap is a plain HashMap of HashSets mutated from raider ticks in different cells
claim: A Raid spans a village (radius ~96 blocks), several 128-block cells wide, but its membership index is 'private final Map<Integer, Set<Raider>> groupRaiderMap = Maps.newHashMap()' (Raid.java:88) with Sets.newHashSet() values. Two entry points into it fire from inside a raider's own entity tick, not from the serial Raids.tick: Raider.aiStep (Raider.java:82-95) calls raid1.joinRaid(...) -> addWaveMob -> 'groupRaiderMap.computeIfAbsent(wave, Sets::newHashSet)' then set.add (Raid.java:670-671), and Raider.die (Raider.java:110-129) calls raid.removeFromRaid(this, false) -> set.remove (Raid.java:588-590). Skein ticks raiders in the parallel entity phase and the margin argument buys nothing here: the write target is a shared object, not a block or an entity section.
scenario: A raid is running with ~20 raiders spread across a village. Raid.tick has already ejected several stragglers (Raid.java:469-471, removeFromRaid with wanderedOutOfRaid=true), so those have currentRaid == null. The rejoin check in Raider.aiStep is gated on 'this.level().getGameTime() % 20L == 0L' -- a level-wide clock identical for every raider -- so on every twentieth tick ALL ejected raiders that have wandered back inside the bounds attempt joinRaid in the same tick. Two of them, 80 blocks apart, are in different cells of the same pass and both run groupRaiderMap.computeIfAbsent(wave, ...) / set.add(raider) concurrently. A concurrent HashSet.add loses one insertion, so Raid.getTotalRaidersAlive (Raid.java:584, summing set sizes) undercounts and Raid.tick decides the wave is cleared, advancing or ending the raid with live raiders still attacking. If the concurrent adds instead land during a HashMap/HashSet resize, the next serial iteration of groupRaiderMap.values() in Raid.tick (Raid.java:443) walks a corrupted bucket chain and the level-owning thread spins forever. The die() path reaches the same set: two raiders killed in the same tick by two different iron golems (each kill runs inside its own golem's entity tick, on its own cell thread) both run set.remove.
fix: Mixin net.minecraft.world.entity.raid.Raid and take one per-Raid ReentrantLock across addWaveMob, removeFromRaid, removeLeader, getTotalRaidersAlive and the groupRaiderMap iterations in tick/updateBossbar. It stays a leaf as long as joinRaid's level.addFreshEntityWithPassengers branch (only taken when isRecruited is false, i.e. from the serial Raid.tick) is left outside the lock. Cheaper alternative if a lock is unwanted: make groupRaiderMap a ConcurrentHashMap with ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet() values -- that fixes the structural corruption though not the read-modify-write of totalHealth. Blacklisting raider entity types is only a workaround, since Raid.tick is not the racing party.
evidence: Raid.java:88 'private final Map<Integer, Set<Raider>> groupRaiderMap = Maps.newHashMap()', :669-671 addWaveMob computeIfAbsent + get, :443 tick iterating groupRaiderMap.values(), :469-471 removeFromRaid for stragglers, :584 getTotalRaidersAlive, :587-601 removeFromRaid with set.remove. Raider.java:82-95 aiStep -> joinRaid gated on getGameTime() % 20L == 0L, :110-129 die -> removeFromRaid. Skein: core/EntityTicker.java:52-66 pins only multipart entities, riding stacks, players and the ender_dragon blacklist entry.

title: Cross-level getChunk from a worker takes vanilla's off-thread branch and deadlocks the barrier
claim: `skein$currentOwner` only reports ownership for `TickContext.owns(this.level)`. When a worker touches a *different* level's chunk source, the redirect hands back the real `mainThread`, so `original.call(...)` inside `skein$guardChunkFetch` enters vanilla's `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(..., this.mainThreadProcessor).join()` branch — while the worker is holding that foreign level's `skein$chunkLoadLock`. Nothing drains that level's `mainThreadProcessor` during a pass, so the join never returns and the barrier never closes. This is not hypothetical mod behaviour: vanilla's own portal code does a cross-level `getChunk` from inside an entity tick.
scenario: Default config, entity phase on. A pig stands in an overworld nether portal. Worker W1 ticks it: `Entity.baseTick` (mcsrc Entity.java:448) → `handlePortal()` (Entity.java:2270-2277) → `NetherPortalBlock.getPortalDestination` (NetherPortalBlock.java:130-141) resolves `serverlevel` = THE NETHER → `PortalForcer.findClosestPortalPosition` (PortalForcer.java:41-44) → `PoiManager.ensureLoadedAndValid` (PoiManager.java:260-268) → `levelReader.getChunk(x, z, ChunkStatus.EMPTY)` on the nether for up to 17x17 columns. In `skein$guardChunkFetch`, `local.deferring` is true, `chunkMap.getVisibleChunkIfPresent` returns null for an unloaded column, so line 225 takes the NETHER's `skein$chunkLoadLock` and line 228 calls `original.call`. There, the `skein$currentOwner` redirect evaluates `TickContext.owns(netherLevel)` — false, because `W1.local.level == overworld` — and returns `this.mainThread`, so vanilla (ServerChunkCache.java:136-138) does `supplyAsync(..., mainThreadProcessor).join()`. That queue is drained only by `MinecraftServer.pollTaskInternal` (MinecraftServer.java:863-873) — the server thread is parked inside `SkeinPool.invokeAll`'s wait loop and never calls it (and during a dimension phase `MinecraftServerMixin.skein$holdTasksDuringPhase` short-circuits it to false anyway) — or by the nether's owner inside its own `managedBlock`. The moment W2 (ticking the nether) needs to load a chunk it blocks on the lock W1 is holding, so the last possible drainer is gone. Hard deadlock; `SkeinPool.reportStall` dumps stacks after 10s and the server hangs silently.
fix: Make the ownership answer include "holds this level's chunk lock": in `skein$currentOwner` return `Thread.currentThread()` when `TickContext.owns(this.level) || ((SkeinLevel) this.level).skein$chunkLoadLock().isHeldByCurrentThread()`. `skein$guardChunkFetch` already establishes that exclusion before calling `original.call`, so vanilla then takes its main-thread branch on the calling thread and drives `mainThreadProcessor.managedBlock` itself — no cross-thread handoff, no deadlock. Additionally skip the fast path (and `skein$parkTicket`) entirely when `this.level != TickContext.current()`, and go straight to the lock, so a foreign level's ticket is never parked in this level's buffer.
evidence: mcsrc ServerChunkCache.java:136-141 (off-thread branch), 863-873 in MinecraftServer.java (only drainer), PortalForcer.java:41-44, PoiManager.java:260-268 (`levelReader.getChunk(...ChunkStatus.EMPTY)`), NetherPortalBlock.java:130-141, Entity.java:448/2270-2282. Skein: ServerChunkCacheMixin.java:156-157, 223-237; MinecraftServerMixin.java:76-81; SkeinPool.java:144-163.

title: ServerLevel.onBlockStateChange is the one setBlock-path structural write left undeferred, and PoiManager is unsynchronised
claim: `Level.markAndNotifyBlock` ends with `this.onBlockStateChange(pos, old, new)`; `ServerLevel`'s override mutates the level-wide `PoiManager`. Skein defers every other level-wide write on that path (`sendBlockUpdated`, `blockEvent`, `addEntity`, `LevelTicks.schedule`, ticker registration) but not this one. `PoiManager`/`SectionStorage` is a plain `Long2ObjectOpenHashMap` plus a `LongLinkedOpenHashSet` whose *read* paths write (`getOrLoad` → `storage.put`, `setDirty` → `dirty.add`, `take` → `acquireTicket`), and it is reached from the entity phase and from `ServerLevel.tickChunk` on the default-on random-tick path.
scenario: `ServerLevel.onBlockStateChange` (mcsrc ServerLevel.java:1443-1457) wraps the POI update in `this.getServer().execute(...)`. `MinecraftServer extends ReentrantBlockableEventLoop`, and `BlockableEventLoop.execute` (BlockableEventLoop.java:95-101) runs the task **inline** when `scheduleExecutables()` is false, i.e. when `isSameThread() && !runningTask()` (ReentrantBlockableEventLoop.java:11-13). While the server thread runs a cell as `SkeinPool.invokeAll`'s caller-runs participant it is `isSameThread()` and `reentrantCount == 0`, so the POI write executes inline mid-pass. Interleaving: server thread runs cell A, a zombie breaks a bed → `Level.setBlock` → `markAndNotifyBlock` → `onBlockStateChange` → inline `poiManager.remove(pos)` → `SectionStorage.getOrLoad` (`storage.get`/`storage.put`, SectionStorage.java:76-115) and `PoiSection.remove` → `setDirty` → `dirty.add`. Concurrently worker W1 runs cell B 200 blocks away, ticks a villager → `AcquirePoi` → `PoiManager.getInChunk` (PoiManager.java:97-102) → `getOrLoad` on a not-yet-loaded POI section → `readColumn` → `storage.put` and a rehash. A `Long2ObjectOpenHashMap` get racing a rehash returns a wrong `Optional` or spins forever in its linear probe — which presents as the barrier never closing. A second, phase-independent instance: two thunderstruck chunks in different cells of the random-tick pass both hit `ServerLevel.tickChunk` → `findLightningTargetAround` → `findLightningRod` → `poiManager.findClosest(..., 128, ANY)` (ServerLevel.java:483-486, 585-596) → `getOrLoad` from two threads at once, with no server thread involved at all.
fix: Two changes. (1) Add `@Inject(method = "onBlockStateChange", at = @At("HEAD"), cancellable = true)` to `ServerLevelMixin` alongside the existing deferrals, parking `self.onBlockStateChange(pos.immutable(), oldState, newState)` in the `DeferredBuffer` when `TickContext.deferring()`. (2) `PoiManager` is level-wide mutable state on a tick path and needs the same treatment as `RedstoneTorchBlock.RECENT_TOGGLES`: a `PoiManagerMixin`/`SectionStorageMixin` that takes one per-level lock around `getOrLoad`, `getOrCreate`, `setDirty` and `PoiSection` mutation, or blacklist villagers/bees from the entity phase and guard the lightning-rod lookup.
