Skein: `grep -rni poi src/` returns nothing — PoiManager is not handled anywhere.

title: DeferredWork.defer ignores its level argument, so a cross-level write is replayed by the wrong coordinator
claim: `defer(Level level, Runnable action)` never uses `level`; it parks into `TickContext.buffer()`, which is the buffer of the cell the *calling* thread is running. Every caller assumes the write belongs to the level being ticked, but three of them can be handed a foreign level: `ServerLevelMixin.skein$deferSpawn` (via `Entity.changeDimension`), `ServerChunkCacheMixin.skein$parkTicket`, and `LevelTicksMixin.skein$deferSchedule`. The foreign level's structural write is then applied by the *source* level's coordinator, at the source level's barrier, while the destination level is being ticked concurrently — which is precisely the corruption the deferral machinery exists to prevent.
scenario: Dimension phase active: W1 ticks the overworld, W2 ticks the nether. A minecart sits in an overworld nether portal whose destination chunks are already loaded (so finding 1's deadlock is skipped). W1: `Entity.handlePortal` → `Entity.changeDimension(transition)` → `serverlevel1.addDuringTeleport(entity2)` (mcsrc Entity.java:2745) → `ServerLevel.addDuringTeleport` → `ServerLevel.addEntity` on the NETHER. `ServerLevelMixin.skein$deferSpawn` sees `TickContext.deferring() == true` and parks `netherLevel.addFreshEntity(entity)` into W1's *overworld* cell buffer. `ParallelPass.run` (line 83) drains that buffer on the overworld's coordinator the moment the overworld's pass closes — but the nether's own pass/tick is still running on W2. The replay calls `PersistentEntitySectionManager.addNewEntity` on the nether, writing `EntityLookup`'s id and uuid maps and `EntitySectionStorage`'s section map and sorted section-id set while W2 iterates them to answer area queries. Same shape for `skein$parkTicket`: a `DistanceManager.addTicket` for the nether is replayed by the overworld's coordinator into the nether's distance manager.
fix: Make the level argument load-bearing: in `DeferredWork.target()`, return the buffer only when `level == TickContext.current()`. For a foreign level there is no safe buffer, so the correct answer is to keep such work off the parallel path — pin entities with a live `portalProcess` in `EntityTicker.isPinned` (an `@Accessor` on `Entity.portalProcess`), and have `skein$parkTicket`/`skein$deferSchedule` fall back to the inline path under that level's own lock when `level != TickContext.current()`.
evidence: Skein DeferredWork.java:34-42 and 68-70 (the `level` parameter is dead); ServerLevelMixin.java:67-74; ServerChunkCacheMixin.java:240-245; LevelTicksMixin.java:73-87 (it even fetches `TickContext.current()` rather than the container's own level); ParallelPass.java:82-84. mcsrc Entity.java:2719-2748 (`serverlevel1.addDuringTeleport`), ServerLevel.java:907-913, 939-951.

title: Per-level ThreadLocal neighbour updaters retain every unloaded Level for the life of the worker pool
claim: `skein$neighborUpdaters` is a `ThreadLocal` field owned by the `Level`, and its value is a `CollectingNeighborUpdater` that holds `private final Level level` (mcsrc CollectingNeighborUpdater.java:17). That is the textbook `ThreadLocal` leak cycle: the `ThreadLocalMap.Entry` key is a weak ref to the `ThreadLocal`, but the entry's *value* strongly reaches the `Level`, which strongly reaches the `ThreadLocal`. The key is therefore never cleared, the entry is never expunged, and the whole `ServerLevel` graph is pinned in every Skein worker that ever ticked it, until the pool is shut down at `ServerStoppingEvent`. All the other per-thread state in the mod correctly lives on `TickContext.Local` instead.
scenario: A dedicated server with a dynamic-dimension mod (RFTools-style dimensions, dungeon dimensions, per-party instances). Each generated `ServerLevel` is ticked at least once by every worker, so every worker's `ThreadLocalMap` gains an entry holding that level's `CollectingNeighborUpdater`. The dimension is later unloaded and dropped from `MinecraftServer.levels`, but with 16 workers there are 16 strong roots to it: `Worker.threadLocals → Entry.value → CollectingNeighborUpdater.level → ServerLevel → ChunkMap → every ChunkHolder/LevelChunk/entity it still referenced`. Nothing ever clears them because the weak key stays strongly reachable through the cycle, so heap use grows monotonically with the number of dimensions created and the server OOMs after a long session. The same applies on an integrated server across world switches within one process.
fix: Move the per-thread updater off the `Level`-owned `ThreadLocal` and onto `TickContext.Local`, keyed by level — e.g. a small `IdentityHashMap<Level, NeighborUpdater>` (or a one-entry cache, since a thread ticks one level at a time) on `Local`, cleared in `TickContext.exit`. If the `ThreadLocal` is kept, have `ParallelPass.runCell` call `skein$neighborUpdaters.remove()` in its `finally`, or make the value hold a `WeakReference<Level>`.
evidence: Skein LevelMixin.java:91-92 and 134-135 (`ThreadLocal.withInitial(() -> new CollectingNeighborUpdater(self, maxChainedNeighborUpdates))`, field on the Level), 162-164. mcsrc CollectingNeighborUpdater.java:15-26 (`private final Level level`). Skein.java:75/88-92 shows the pool lives for the whole server session, so nothing collects the worker threads in the meantime. Contrast TickContext.java:40-73, where every other per-thread copy is held on `Local`.
